active_relay_test.important_result: The reader can follow a running story without completing a protagonist roster. The relay may stop and remain with one actor for multiple chapters.

relay_rule: Story order is not chosen to introduce protagonists evenly. One event leaves a concrete destination, relationship, task, consequence or unresolved process; the camera follows that relay. A new core actor appears only when the active story naturally reaches them. Relay is not itself a quota: once the story reaches a character, it may remain there for several chapters.
arc_rendering_rule: Campbell structures a character longitudinally after the story reaches that character. Campbell stages never determine who must appear next. Foreground prose remains partial, visual, fallible and under-explained.
character_entrance_rule: First substantial appearance is scene-first and event-first, but no actor is owed a standalone entrance chapter. An actor may first appear inside someone else's active story and become focal only later.
nonnegotiable_rules: No adaptation hypothesis becomes ledger history.
Do not introduce a core actor because the roster says it is their turn.
Do not require all six core actors to appear in the opening movement or Part 1.
A chapter transition must be explainable by a concrete relay: consequence, person, task, message, place, public process or existing relationship.
Do not force a baton handoff every chapter; remaining with the same focal actor is valid when the live problem continues.
Same theme or same generation alone does not count as story connection.
A relay may branch, but prose follows one branch at a time; other branches may stay offstage for chapters.
Secondary and guest characters may carry the narrative baton between core actors.
Early chapters should normally add no more than one or two memorable names at a time.
Use role labels for nonrecurring guests until a name matters.
Background leaks through action, dialogue, objects, institutions, money, space and other people's reactions rather than profile paragraphs.
High education does not imply universal negotiation, leadership, emotional or social skill.
Every strong capability must have a formation source, shadow cost and high-pressure failure mode.
A virtue must be allowed to create costs; a flaw must be allowed to protect something real.
Power changes how personality is expressed; separate trait from position effect.
Campbell stages are backend structure only and never chapter labels, thesis dialogue or explicit self-diagnosis.
Character transformation changes probabilities, thresholds and recovery patterns; it does not permanently remove old flaws.
Every core actor retains at least one materially unresolved ambiguity at the 2035 horizon.
Do not force romance, illness, family disaster, betrayal, crime or redemption to manufacture a hook.
Do not imitate Water Margin through archaic diction or chapter-title pastiche; borrow its relay mechanics and event-driven entrances only.
Do not use AI-summary endings, thesis dialogue, forced symbolism or universal self-awareness.
2035 is an observation endpoint, not a life verdict.
relay_audit_questions: What concrete thing from the previous scene makes the camera move here?
Why does the story need this person now?
Would this actor still enter if their core-character label were hidden?
What does the newcomer want independently of the previous focal actor?
Does the current live problem still deserve another chapter before any handoff?
What changes or remains unresolved that can push the story onward?
How many new names is the reader being asked to retain?
